subject: Follow-up: Context length profiling & pricing (ACME)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Context length profiling & pricing (ACME)

Hey Alex -

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap + next steps from our discovery call so we have alignment on pricing inputs:

Key notes from call:
- Primary workload: automated customer support summarization + triage and a smaller set of assisted-authoring features for CS reps.
- Typical request shape (rough): multi-turn prompt that includes a conversation transcript + instruction + metadata.
- Goal: keep latency < 500ms p95 for interactive flows; batch/async for background summarization is okay.

Questions we called out that impact pricing:
1) Average prompt tokens and completion tokens per request (if you have p50/p90/p99 distributions, even better).
2) Monthly request volume and expected ramp over 3/6/12 months.
3) Percent of requests that need longer context (8k vs 32k vs 128k) - and example transcript sizes.
4) Target $/1M tokens (budget range) and any procurement constraints/training period.

From our side I attached a short pricing deck and an example CSV template for context-length profiling - if you can drop a few rows of sample stats we can produce a tailored estimate (unit economics with/without KV-prefix caching and quantized model variants).

Attachments: [Attachment: Redwood_pricing_deck_ACME_v2.pdf] [Attachment: context-length-sample-stats.csv]

Next steps proposed:
- You: share token-length distribution (sample or aggregated) + rough monthly volumes by 6/14.
- Us: produce 2 pricing options (low-latency interactive and cost-optimized async) and a short mutual action plan by 6/16.

If you want, we can also run a short profiler on a 7-10 day sample to validate real token counts - likely useful if you have long transcripts.

Thanks -
Marissa

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Context length profiling & pricing (ACME)

Marissa -

Appreciate the recap. Quick answers from our side (high level, will follow up with a CSV):
- Avg prompt tokens (p50/p90/p99): ~1,200 / 2,800 / 12,000 tokens. Prompt includes transcript + system instruction.
- Avg completion tokens (p50/p90/p99): ~800 / 1,800 / 6,000 tokens.
- Monthly requests today: ~50k. Expected pilot (Q3): 50k/mo, ramp to ~300k/mo by Q4 with full rollout 1H27.
- Token estimate (approx): current baseline ~ (1,200+800)*50k ≈ 100M tokens/mo. Peak rollout ≈ 600M tokens/mo.
- Long-context needs: ~5% of requests exceed 32k and require up to ~60k tokens (meeting transcripts). The majority are under 8k.
- Budget / target $/1M tokens: ops and leadership would prefer ~$20–$40 / 1M tokens depending on latency SLA. For pilot we have a small budget (low thousands/mo) but can expand.

We will export aggregated token-length histograms and drop into your CSV by EOD 6/14. Also looping procurement for contract/PO timing.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Director, AI Platform - ACME Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com | +1 617-555-0987

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-13T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Context length profiling & pricing (ACME)

Alex -

This is super helpful, thanks. A few clarifying items so we size the options correctly:
- When you say ~5% exceed 32k, is that evenly distributed between 32k–64k and 64k–128k, or clustered near ~50–60k? (helps us pick an efficient 32k vs 128k strategy).
- For the 600M tokens/mo peak scenario, are those primarily read-heavy (large prompts, small completions) or write-heavy (large completions)? Your note suggests balanced but we want to confirm (impacts batching and unit cost).

What we'll do once we have the CSV:
- Provide two cost models: "interactive" (latency-first; higher $/1M tokens, p95 latency SLO) and "cost-optimized" (batching, quantized models, more aggressive caching).
- Show delta per 1M tokens at p50/p95 token mix, and a blended monthly cost for the volumes you provided.

If you can include one or two example transcripts (redacted) we can run a short profiler that outputs exact prompt/completion token lengths and a recommended context-tier mix (8k/32k/128k) - will take us ~48 hours to run and validate.

Attached: I dropped a sample CSV template (context-length-sample-stats.csv).

Will give you the pricing options by 6/16.

Thanks -
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-13T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: ACME — context-length & pricing (need approval for pilot discount)

Jordan / Marcus -

Forwarding the thread with ACME. They gave initial volume ramps and called out ~5% of requests that need up to ~60k tokens. Pilot expected at 50k/mo moving to 300k/mo. Target $/1M tokens $20–$40 (ops preference).

Ask: can we offer a pilot price of $18 / 1M tokens for the first 3 months (capped to 150M tokens) to get them through PoC? After pilot, move to tiered pricing with volume discounts. I recommend including a short profiling add-on (one-time) to validate context-tier mix - cost-covered by Redwood for the pilot.

Reasoning:
- Pilot helps us validate long-context behavior and shows value quickly.
- 5% long-context makes a big difference - if we can show caching + sparse 128k usage we win.

If approved, I'll send a short MSA + pilot addendum and the pricing summary for procurement.

Thanks -
Marissa

(On approval we should prepare a PoC mutual action plan and a DocuSign-ready quote.)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: ACME PoC proposal & next steps (pricing summary)

Alex / Procurement -

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the numbers. Based on the profiling info you shared, here's a concise proposal and mutual action plan:

1) Pilot (PoC) - 6 weeks
- Scope: validate support summarization pipeline with up to 150M tokens (capped) and profiling on long transcripts.
- Pricing: $18 / 1M tokens for pilot months (applied to actual usage, capped at 150M).
- Add-ons: one-time profiling run (48–72 hours) - free during pilot.

2) Post-pilot (recommended tiering)
- 0–200M tokens/mo: $30 / 1M tokens
- 200–500M tokens/mo: $25 / 1M tokens
- 500M+ tokens/mo: custom enterprise pricing (includes SLA & dedicated routing).

3) Context-tier guidance (from profiler):
- ~85% of requests: 8k context adequate.
- ~10%: 32k context preferred.
- ~5%: 64k–128k requests (meeting transcripts) - we recommend using KV-prefix caching + batching to reduce unit costs here.

Next steps today:
- ACME to send the aggregated CSV (we received a sample) and two redacted transcripts for the profiler.
- Procurement to confirm PO timeline and whether a 3-month pilot is acceptable.
- I will share a DocuSign quote (pilot MSA + pilot addendum) by EOD - link below.

DocuSign (quote): https://app.redwood.com/docusign/ACME-quote-2026
HubSpot deal: https://redwood.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-Q3-01

If these terms look reasonable I can send the pilot DocuSign now and we can kick off profiling immediately.

Best -
